claims.object_text: encodes the pore-forming subunits of the KV1.2 channel that controls excitability of central and peripheral neurons
claims.quote: KCNA2 encodes the pore-forming subunits of the voltage-gated, potassium-selective channel KV1.2, which controls the excitability of both central and peripheral neurons.
Either gain- or loss-of-function KCNA2 variants can cause severe neurological disease, assigned developmental epileptic encephalopathy (DEE) type 32.
p.H310D and p.G318D, both discovered in patients with global developmental delay
We found that both are loss-of-function variants, completely abolishing channel current and subunit trafficking.

claims.object_text: shifted half-activation potentials by 27 and 19 mV for p.H310D and p.G318D
claims.quote: Channel constructs of KV1.2-variant subunits in tandem with KV1.4 had a conductance with inhibited voltage-dependence, with shifted half-activation potentials by 27 and 19 mV for p.H310D and p.G318D, respectively.
p.H310D was strongly negative-dominant: heterozygous cells exhibited only 7% conductance relative to homozygous wild-type, while only half of wild-type subunits could traffic to the surface.
In contrast, p.G318D exhibited weaker negative dominance, with 32% conductance in heterozygous cells and 86% wild-type-subunit trafficking.
Taken together with the p.G318D-patient's neurological symptoms, the latter suggests that KCNA2 is a haploinsufficient gene in humans.
